what: NDT-GEMM-L1 and NDT-BETA (2026-10-16): where the AVX-512 blocked kernel's time goes against the FMA probe -- the inner loop alone over one packed tile at depths 64-448, the pack's and the beta pass's cycles inside a task of the pool's partition, fourteen variants that keep the arithmetic -- and the slice that removed the beta pass: the blocked kernels scale C by beta in their first K block's epilogue (under beta 0 the terms added to +0.0 without reading C, under any other beta the loaded C scaled by the same rounded product), every element the one it was.
host: 4-vCPU Intel Xeon @ 2.80GHz container (AVX-512; the instance after the 2026-10-16 restart, slower in this session than in §17's), GCC 13.3 (the trainer builds), Python 3.11.15 (the declared floor); indicative wall times, no PMU

files.gemm_probe.c, probe-ceiling.jsonl, probe: the probe, built against ad77c84's unit (it includes the unit whole, so its static kernels are reachable, and scales c itself before each task, as the unit did before this slice): the inner loop alone over one tile at depths 64..448 with A's rows 448 or 1024 floats apart (ceiling); every variant over the step's twelve GEMM shapes at one thread and on a pool of four, interleaved round by round in one process, each variant's C compared with the kernel's bit for bit (identical: true on every line), median_ms a call; the pack's and the beta pass's shares of a one-thread task's cycles (rdtsc)
files.gemm_entries.c, entries-t1.jsonl, entrie: the step's twelve GEMM shapes through bcir_tensor_mm_kblock (one thread) and bcir_tensor_mm_kblock_pool (four), at the betas the trainer passes, built against ad77c84's runtime/c/bcir_tensor.c (build ad77c84) and this slice's (build ndt-beta), the two builds alternated in twelve rounds; median_ms of nine repetitions per shape and round, c_fnv1a an FNV-1a digest of C (equal across the builds and the rounds for every shape)
files.attribution-t4-before-{1..4}.json, attri: the step in place at four threads (docs/research/measurements/2026-10-13/scan/attribution.py --src TREE/runtime/c --data DATA --threads 4 --steps 8): before = ad77c84, beta = ad77c84 with this slice's runtime/c/bcir_tensor.c; alternated round by round with a third arm, this slice with NDT-SCHED-1 (../sched1/), four rounds; rows_ms is each category's milliseconds per step over the eight steps, step_wall_ms_median the step's median
files.identity.json: the 20-step state at one and four threads under kblock+exp+reduce for the widest, AVX2-capped and portable builds (train_comparison.py identity --steps 20 --threads 1,4 --contract kblock+exp+reduce --variants widest,avx2,portable): every row 4bf4e057..., the state before the slice

reading: The kernel's inner loop alone runs at 162.1-170.9 GFLOP/s over depths 64-448 (the FMA probe's 162-165 a thread): the contract's depth and the tile's L2 residence cost nothing. A one-thread task's pack is 5.6-12.6% of its cycles and its beta pass 1.6-8.9%. No variant moved beyond one run's noise (256-row tasks -2.0% / -6.7% at one / four threads, the pack's 16-row prefetch +1.0% / -5.5%, the two together -1.3% / -1.6%). With the pass folded into the first K block: the step's GEMM shapes alone at four threads 198.6 -> 175.3 ms a step (medians of twelve alternated rounds, 10 faster; by each shape's minimum 162.1 -> 144.8), at one thread 551.3 -> 546.7 (7 of 12; 466.7 -> 464.7), the gate and up input adjoint (depth 1024, beta 0) slower at both counts (4% at one, 3-12% at four); in place at four threads the GEMMs 199.6 -> 179.5 ms a step (every round of four), the step 267.8 -> 254.2.
